events.title: First National Thanksgiving Day in the United States
events.description: Following a proclamation by President George Washington, Americans observed the first national Thanksgiving Day under the new Constitution, set aside as a day of public thanksgiving and prayer for the favorable conclusion of the American Revolution and the establishment of the new government.
events.significance: Established a precedent for national days of thanksgiving, which later evolved into the annual U.S. holiday formally set by Abraham Lincoln in 1863.

events.title: Howard Carter Enters the Tomb of Tutankhamun
events.description: British archaeologist Howard Carter, financed by Lord Carnarvon, looked through a small breach in the sealed doorway of Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings and, asked if he could see anything, famously replied 'Yes, wonderful things.'
events.significance: The discovery of the nearly intact tomb of the pharaoh became one of the most important archaeological finds in history and sparked worldwide fascination with ancient Egypt.

events.title: Premiere of the Film Casablanca
events.description: The Warner Bros. film Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman and directed by Michael Curtiz, had its world premiere in New York City, shortly after the Allied landings in North Africa.
events.significance: The film won the Academy Award for Best Picture and is widely regarded as one of the greatest films in cinema history.

events.title: India's Constituent Assembly Adopts the Constitution
events.description: The Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution of India, drafted under the chairmanship of B. R. Ambedkar, after nearly three years of deliberation. It came into force on January 26, 1950.
events.significance: The adoption laid the foundation for the world's largest democracy; the date is commemorated in India as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas).

events.title: Brink's-Mat Robbery at Heathrow Airport
events.description: Armed robbers broke into the Brink's-Mat warehouse near London's Heathrow Airport and stole about 6,800 kg of gold bullion, diamonds, and cash, worth roughly 26 million pounds at the time.
events.significance: Dubbed the 'crime of the century' in Britain, it led to long-running investigations and money-laundering cases, and little of the gold was ever recovered.
